node.title: Re^6: Begginer's question: If loops one after the other. Is that code correct?
node.author: choroba
node.doctext:
You can simplify the code by removing the special cases for the two-character combinations and just use a regex. Just make sure you try to match the longer "characters" first, so their parts aren't matched instead.

Also, I used [METAMOD://XML::LibXML] to parse the structure.

#!/usr/bin/perl use warnings; use strict; use utf8; use XML::LibXML; my $file = shift; my %to_cyrilic = ( # Insert the hash definition here, see below. ); my $regex = join '|', sort { length $b <=> length $a } keys %to_cyrilic; my $dom = 'XML::LibXML'->load_html( location => $file ); for my $text ($dom->findnodes('//text()')) { my $etext = $text; $text->setData($etext) if $etext =~ s/($regex)/$to_cyrilic{$1}/g; } print $dom;

Note that PRE tags preserve non-latin1 characters.
